acceptance: The collector partitions the requested UTC interval into searches below the API result limit (GitHub caps filtered workflow-run searches at 1,000 results), exhausts pagination, deduplicates boundary records, and fetches every run attempt and its jobs. Tests cover more than 1,000 results, partition boundaries, partial reruns, and retrieval failure. Incomplete retrieval cannot produce an unqualified success report.
A single make target, built on _project/scripts/dev_loop_pr_metrics.py, produces the report for a given --since/--until window with no run-count cap

The report includes per-workflow and per-event run counts and conclusions, rerun-attempt outcomes, all-attempt runner-minutes, and job queue time (created to started, skipped jobs excluded) median and p90. A test shows that the wait before a rerun attempt is not counted as queue time.

Required contexts are resolved from the live develop ruleset (currently core, docs, explorer, results-data, tooling, hold, oracle-gate) and recorded with provenance; a test covers a ruleset that differs from the built-in list and a historical window in which oracle-gate was not yet required, using an explicit stated rule.

Report per-PR/head time-to-green from an observed head-update event to all applicable required check-runs and commit statuses being successful, including the App-bound oracle-gate. Record context-policy provenance, timestamp source, missing observations, and unresolved or censored heads. Report CI-compute-ready separately from all-required-checks-ready. Any proxy (for example commit author time or workflow creation time) is labelled as a proxy.

Report all-attempt runner-minutes per PR lifecycle and per merge, alongside per-run values; separate text edits, code and non-code routing, heavy-tier reasons, event, runner OS, and cancelled work. Every comparison includes sample counts, collection completeness, and workload composition.

The report includes the post-merge signal-quality figures: first-attempt red rate, eventual-success rate, distinct incident count, time from first red to recovery, merges admitted during each red incident, age of the newest tested develop commit, and missing or duplicate exact-SHA Trunk runs.

A baseline report for 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-24 (or the longest window still within log and API retention) is recorded on this item, stating which parts are incomplete (for example Trunk coverage runs exist only from 2026-10-21, and artifacts expire after 7, 14 or 30 days)

description: CI efficiency decisions currently rest on ad hoc gh run list samples capped at 1,000 runs (the CI sample and the all-workflow sample each hold exactly 1,000 records, so both are truncated; the 'one-day' all-workflow sample covers only about 14 hours of 2026-10-24) and on job data from the 40 newest runs. The sampling and truncation bias is unquantified. Extend the existing collector _project/scripts/dev_loop_pr_metrics.py (paginated API client, required-check timing, successful/failed/cancelled runner-minute accounting, event fan-out report) and add a make target, instead of building a second framework. Reuse does not mean accepting its definitions unchanged: its 'queue delay' is green-to-merge delay, not runner queue time; its REQUIRED_CONTEXT_NAMES list (lines 36-42) holds five contexts and omits hold and the App-posted oracle-gate; and its lifecycle job lookup does not enumerate the jobs of every run attempt. Required contexts must be read from the live develop ruleset at collection time (gh api repos/BenchBox-dev/benchbox/rules/branches/develop), not hard-coded; on 2026-10-25 they are core, docs, explorer, results-data, tooling, hold and oracle-gate (oracle-review stopped being required in PR #3395). Runner queue time means job created-to-started for each job attempt; subtracting run createdAt from startedAt is not queue time, because the interval includes the first execution and the wait before a rerun (run 39349624872: attempt 2 started 748 minutes after the run was created, but attempt 1 had started immediately). For a given date window the report covers, per workflow and event: run count and conclusions (including runs that passed only on a rerun attempt), summed job runner-minutes across all attempts, job queue time median and p90, and PR time-to-green median and p90. It also reports post-merge signal quality: first-attempt red rate, eventual-success rate, distinct red incidents, time from first red result to recovery, merges admitted during each red incident, age of the newest tested develop commit, and missing or duplicate exact-SHA Trunk runs. A low red rate reached by missing runs, dropped coverage or quarantine is not an improvement. The repository is public, so GitHub-hosted runner minutes are free; the binding limit is the concurrency cap. Queue time and PR time-to-green are the primary success metrics, runner-minutes secondary. Collect locally or on demand; do not add frequent CI work to produce the report.
